movement_source: row 'Net interest margin (%)', column FY20 -> column FY21
headline: CBA Group net interest margin fell 4 bps in FY21, from 207 bps (2.07%) in FY20 to 203 bps (2.03%), per the profit announcement KPI table and stated narrative. The fall was driven by higher liquid asset balances (-4 bps), deposit pricing and funding (-3 bps), asset pricing competition (-2 bps) and capital/other (-2 bps), partly offset by basis risk including replicating portfolio (+3 bps), Treasury and Markets (+2 bps) and favourable portfolio mix (+2 bps). Note the half-on-half move was +3 bps to 2.04%, a different comparison. The Group margin row carries no basis label and is reported on the primary basis.

drivers.narrative: Largest single drag. Growth in liquid asset balances at low yields compressed margin; corroborated by the coarser p29 walk and the profit announcement narrative citing higher liquid assets.
Reduced earnings on transaction and savings balances from cash-rate cuts; narrative also cites lower wholesale funding costs as a partial offset within funding.
Lending margin compression, including ongoing home loan competition, discounting and switching, per the p29 slide commentary.
Lower earnings on equity and replicating portfolio in the falling rate environment; the p29 slide separately shows replicating portfolio at -1 bps for the year.

Favourable funding mix: deposit funding ratio rose from 71% to 77% on TFF drawdown and switching to at-call deposits (+4 bps), partly offset by unfavourable asset mix (-2 bps) from declining consumer finance balances.
Favourable bills/OIS basis movement including replicating portfolio effects was the largest positive contributor to the year-on-year margin walk.
Markets and Treasury contribution supported margin, consistent with divisional slides citing higher Global Markets income on lower funding costs and increased commodities margins.

notable_items: Half-on-half context only: NIM rose 3 bps on the prior half (Dec 2020) to 2.04%, driven partly by portfolio mix +3 bps; this is a different comparison and supplies no FY21 vs FY20 number.
Divisional margin rows (e.g. 2.63% to 2.60%, -3 bps; RBS, IB&M, NZ half-yearly series) are business-unit measures and were excluded from the Group movement.
The Group NIM row carries no cash or statutory label; it is reported on the bank's primary basis and is not statutory.

disagreements.topic: Walk granularity for the same FY20 -> FY21 comparison
values: 3-bar walk: Higher liquids -4, Impact of lower rates -6, Management actions/other +6 (ev-1, p29)
7-bar walk: Higher Liquids -4, Asset Pricing -2, Deposit Pricing & Funding -3, Capital & Other -2, Portfolio Mix +2, Basis Risk (incl RP) +3, Treasury & Markets +2 (ev-2, p63)
disagreements.explanation: Both are presentation slides describing the identical FY20 -> FY21 bridge and both sum to -4 bps. The 7-bar walk is adopted because it is granular and maps to the canonical taxonomy; the 3-bar walk folds rate impacts and management actions into aggregate bars. No results-book walk was in evidence, so the slide walk is the best available framing.

disagreements.topic: Group NIM vs divisional NIM row
disagreements.explanation: The 2.63/2.60 row is a single business unit's margin at a different level; only the Group row supplies the task movement.

disagreements.topic: Comparison span of stated NIM changes
values: FY21 vs FY20: -4 bps to 2.03% (ev-7, ev-10, ev-21, ev-22)
FY21 second half vs prior half: +3 bps to 2.04% (ev-3, ev-4)
disagreements.explanation: The +3 bps movement is half-on-half against Dec 2020, a different question; the task comparison is the full-year -4 bps.

The two presentation records print the same two NII figures with reversed period labels; one record misassigns the years. This does not affect the NIM movement, which is taken from the profit announcement KPI table.

limitations: No results-book (profit announcement) NIM driver walk was in evidence; the driver table is built from the presentation slide walk (ev-2, p63), which passes its sum check and is corroborated in direction and key magnitudes by the coarser slide walk (ev-1) and profit announcement narrative (ev-10).

The 3-bar walk's 'Impact of lower rates' (-6 bps) and 'Management actions/other' (+6 bps) bars do not map to the canonical taxonomy; they are treated as an aggregate framing of the same -4 bps bridge rather than claimed as separate drivers.
The ev-12/ev-20 net interest income label conflict could not be resolved from the available records; it does not enter the margin calculation.
Individual driver bars other than liquids and mix appear in a single document (the p63 slide), so their confidences are capped at 85.

Net interest margin was $9,468 million, an increase of $97 million or 1% on the prior half, driven by a $14 billion or 2% increase in average interest earning assets to $937 billion and a 3 basis point increase in net interest margin to 2.04%, partly offset by the impact of three fewer calendar days in the current half.

evidence_records.quote: The Bank’s net interest margin increased 3 basis points on the prior half to 2.04%. The key drivers of the movement were: ... Portfolio mix: Increased margin by 3 basis points driven by favourable funding mix from the drawdown of the TFF and customers switching to at-call deposits (up 2 basis points), and favourable lending mix from the decline of lower margin institutional lending balances (up 1 basis point).

Portfolio mix: Increased margin by 2 basis points driven by a higher average deposit funding ratio (30 June 2021: 77%; 30 June 2020: 71%) due to strong growth in transaction and savings deposits, customers switching to at-call deposits, and the drawdown of the TFF (up 4 basis points), partly offset by an unfavourable impact from asset mix (down 2 basis points), mainly due to a decline in higher margin consumer finance balances.
